current.text: He played heavy minutes at the end of last season.
He averaged 22.5 points in two Summer League games and shot well.
Washington has a crowded group of young wings and guards, and he is one of them.
Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa, which cuts into the roles of the young players.
He is not in the projected starting five of Young, Kyshawn George, Dybantsa, Davis and Alex Sarr. The fifth starter spot is open, and many wings are competing for it.
The Wizards are expected to use a deep 10 or 11 man rotation, with 12 or 13 players who could justify minutes.
The expert does not expect his value from late last season to return, because Washington has too many wings and guards.
Washington is trying to compete this season, so the expert expects no late-season resting or minutes cuts like in past years.

durable.text: His projected steals are far below the top 250 pool, which makes STL his clearest weak category.
